title: Kumbhakarna
hook: the giant tells his brother he's wrong, and goes to fight for him anyway

segments.voice: Yesterday: Kumbhakarna, the giant who sleeps for months, woken with drums and elephants because Ravana was losing. Did you use a hidden strength on something ordinary? Today, the giant hears what his brother has done. Day six hundred forty-six.

Kumbhakarna walks into Ravana's hall, still huge with sleep, and Ravana pours it all out. Rama has crossed the sea. Our best warriors are dead. I lost today. You're the only one left who can save us. The court waits for the giant's roar. And Kumbhakarna, the brother everyone thinks of as a sleeping appetite, says something no one else in the palace has dared to say this plainly to the king's face.
screen: `RAVANA POURS IT OUT.` → `YOU'RE THE ONLY ONE LEFT.` → `THE GIANT SPEAKS PLAINLY.`

segments.voice: We told you, he says. When you held your council, this is exactly what we said would happen. A king who acts first and thinks afterward, who does what he wants and ignores good advice, brings disaster on himself. You took another man's wife. This is the result. Ravana's face darkens. He doesn't want a lecture; he wants a champion. And Kumbhakarna sees his brother hurting, and softens. Enough, he says. Don't grieve. Whatever you did, I'm your brother. I'll go and kill your enemy. That's the knot at the heart of Kumbhakarna, and it's why so many people love him. He knows Ravana is wrong. He says so, to his face. And then he goes to fight for him anyway, out of loyalty. On the battlefield he's terrifying. The monkeys scatter before him, and Angada has to shame them into turning back. He seizes Sugriva and carries him off under his arm toward the city. Sugriva comes to his senses, tears at the giant's ears and nose, and escapes. In the end Rama faces him, and with his arrows brings him down, and Valmiki says the great head fell on Lanka. The Tamil poet Kamban adds a scene many readers treasure. Before the fight, Vibhishana comes to his brother on the field and begs him to join Rama. Kumbhakarna refuses gently. You did right, he says, more or less; you stay with Rama. My place is with our brother. Some readers see a fool here. Many see one of the most honest characters in the epic: clear about what is right, and bound by love to what is wrong.
screen: `WE TOLD YOU THIS WOULD HAPPEN.` · `STILL, I'M YOUR BROTHER.` · `SUGRIVA UNDER HIS ARM.` · `KAMBAN: YOU STAY WITH RAMA.` · then, large: `CLEAR ABOUT RIGHT, BOUND BY LOVE.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let your breath settle. Think of a time loyalty pulled you one way and your sense of what's right pulled another: a friend, a family member, a team. Don't judge your past self. Just feel both pulls, side by side, the way Kumbhakarna felt them. Breathe in, and let them both be real. Breathe out, and let the knot be a little looser. The bell holds the time.
Kumbhakarna. The giant who tells Ravana plainly he's wrong, and then goes out and dies fighting for him, out of a brother's loyalty.
Your line: Kumbhakarna. Today, if you disagree with someone you love, say it plainly, and stay kind. Day six hundred forty-six.

howItsDone: Kumbhakarna's rebuke of Ravana and his loyalty are much discussed in Ramayana storytelling, and Kamban's Tamil scene of the two brothers, Vibhishana and Kumbhakarna, meeting on the battlefield is often recited.

he tells him plainly it was wrong, and that disaster was predicted.
he fights for Ravana anyway, out of loyalty
he says that whatever Ravana did, he's still his brother.
he comes to his senses, tears at the giant's ears and nose, and gets free.

fork.setup: you're Kumbhakarna. your brother has done wrong, you've told him so, and now he's begging for your help. what do you do?
options: refuse and go back to sleep.
fight for him anyway, because he's your brother.
fork.reveal: he goes out to fight for Ravana, and falls to Rama's arrows.

original.note: Sanskrit bhrātā: brother, from the same Indo-European root as the English word brother.

trapdoor: what you thought: Kumbhakarna is a sleepy monster.
what it means: he tells Ravana the truth to his face, then fights for him out of loyalty.
what a scholar hears: Kamban gives him a farewell scene with Vibhishana that has made him one of the Tamil Ramayana's most loved characters.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 62–63 (Kumbhakarna's rebuke and his promise)
Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 66–67 (Kumbhakarna in battle; Sugriva's escape; Kumbhakarna's death)
Kamba Ramayanam, Yuddha Kandam (Vibhishana meets Kumbhakarna on the battlefield)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.

The head falling on Lanka (some versions add the body falling into the sea): confirm.
